newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt puts on trial 32 financiers for bank frauds.
newsitem.headline: Egypt puts on trial 32 financiers for bank frauds.

text.p: Egypt will put on trial 32 financiers including the chairmen of two private-sector banks for making or taking unsecured loans worth more than one billion pounds ($300 million), government papers said on Wednesday.
The newspaper al-Ahram said prosecutor general Raga el-Arabi sent the 32 to court after endorsing the charges. A date for the trial has yet to be set, the daily added.

The accused include the chairman of Dakhliya Commercial Bank Tawfik Abdou Ismail, Nile Bank chairman Issa el-Ayouti, the deputy directors of Suez Canal Bank and Mohandes Bank and the director of Faisal Islamic Bank.

The daily said that investigations into the charges began in August 1995. Ismail and Ayouti, both members of parliament at the time, had their political immunity lifted and were banned from travelling outside Egypt, it added.
Nile Bank has an authorised capital of 140 million pounds and Dakhaliya Commercial Bank's capital is 100 million.
